title: Visual Proof Paradox: Fake Area Manipulation
full_prompt:
Write a ManimGL script using the InteractiveScene class that visualizes a classic geometric dissection paradox (the 'fake area' or Curry's paradox). The scene should set up a coordinate grid using NumberPlane with a custom unit scale of 0.5. It should display a dissected triangle composed of multiple sub-shapes (represented by two groups of diagrams, group1 and group2). The script must perform the following visual sequence:
1. Initialize a background grid and place the first dissection configuration (group1) along with vertex dots at its corners.
2. Animate a piecewise transformation (using Transform with a curved path_arc) that rearranges the sub-shapes from the first configuration to the second configuration, showing how they seem to form the same overall triangle but with a missing/extra unit of area.
3. Zoom the camera frame in closely onto the hypotenuse boundary of the shape to reveal that the boundary is not a straight line, but rather a slight bend.
4. Restore the camera frame, perform another swap, and zoom in on another critical junction.
5. Draw helper lines representing the actual slopes of the individual sub-triangles (e.g., slopes of 5/2 and 7/3), and label them with text and arrows pointing to the respective slopes to mathematically explain the visual illusion.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Missing definition of get_diagrams helper method
common_failure_modes.note: The reference code relies on self.get_diagrams() which is defined elsewhere in the source file. A complete standalone generation must mock or fully implement the dissection shapes.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Using ManimCE camera syntax instead of ManimGL frame syntax
common_failure_modes.note: ManimGL uses self.camera.frame to zoom and pan, whereas ManimCE uses MovingCameraScene with self.camera.frame. Mixing these up causes runtime crashes.
Using path_arc with invalid angles or incorrect zip unpacking can break the piecewise transition animation.
